See also Middle Dutch telt, Old High German zelt and Old Norse tjald. Cognate with English tilt (“tent fabric and covering”).
Borrowed from Quechua karpa.

From Catalan barraca; see barro.

ex: Our houses are tens of meters apart, so we don't have to worry about noise from our neighbours.
tens of thousands of voters

senses.d: A pair of tens.
The period from a year ending in 10 to a year ending in 19 (mostly referring to the 1910s or 2010s); the teens, the oneties.

From Middle English tenaunt, from Anglo-Norman tenaunt and Old French tenant, present participle of tenir (“to hold”), from Latin tenēre (“hold, keep”).

senses.d: One who holds a lease (a tenancy).
ex: You are just a tenant here, you say / Living in and out of this life / As cheaply as you can
